d07.why: Drops the viewer into a hand they have lived, mid-action, and ends on a question only the reel can answer: bad beat or normal Tuesday?

d03.why: Names a type every player knows and wants to tag, then flips the curse into a counting mistake in two short beats.

d01.why: Opens on the most-felt loss in poker, with a vivid garbage hand, then contradicts the 'rigged' belief the viewer half holds.

d15.why: A one-line truth about memory that any player recognises in themselves, short and quotable.

d20.why: Runner-runner told in three hammer beats lands the pain, and 'nothing' is a dry verdict that disagrees with how the viewer feels.

d16.why: A short-stack scene with real stakes and a promise about the feeling, not the maths, which reaches beyond study-minded viewers.

d05.why: Borrows the angry 'rigged' review everyone has read and promises a number that sides with no one.

d02.why: 79% is a surprising, personal stake (your next ten all-ins), but it is still a stat opening rather than a scene.

d12.why: Denies luck with a hard number and lands a dry closer ('on the schedule'), though it reads closer to a lesson title.

d18.why: The 'you just remember those' turn makes the fact about the viewer, but the opening clause is a textbook line.
